name: hot_plateau_pre_cool_applied
description: Issue #558: a plateaued stretch of hot days (today 91°F, tomorrow 95°F — both hot, but the day-over-day trend magnitude is only +4°F, below TREND_THRESHOLD_MODERATE=5°F) previously got ZERO overnight pre-cool banking, indefinitely, because handle_pre_cool()'s only gate was setback_modifier < 0 (a fresh warming trend). resolve_pre_cool_modifier() now also fires on tomorrow's absolute hot classification (tomorrow_high >= threshold_hot=85) even when setback_modifier stays 0.0, using a flat HOT_DAY_PRE_COOL_MODIFIER=-2.0 fallback so the target isn't a no-op equal to sleep_cool. A setpoint_writes row (Issue #1441) pins the real 70F service call, because the pre_cool_applied event row alone still passed with the write deleted.
notes: Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md §10):
(a) Scenario effectiveness: reverting handle_pre_cool()'s gate to the old
'if not c or c.setback_modifier >= 0: skip' check causes the 02:30 assertion
(expect pre_cool_applied, target=70) to FAIL — the trigger would be skipped entirely
since setback_modifier=0.0 in this scenario.
(b) Docs↔production alignment: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md §4/overnight pre-cool
section must document the hot-day-OR-trend gate and the HOT_DAY_PRE_COOL_MODIFIER
fallback before this scenario is promoted to golden.
(c) Occupant experience: without this fix, a household in a multi-day heat wave with no
single night trending sharply warmer than the last gets no overnight thermal-mass
banking at all, night after night — the AC works harder than necessary each afternoon
purely because the classifier never saw one big jump, only a sustained plateau.
Config: comfort_heat=70, comfort_cool=74 (no explicit sleep_cool/sleep_heat → defaults
DEFAULT_SLEEP_COOL=72.0, DEFAULT_SLEEP_HEAT=64.0 apply).
setback_modifier=0.0 (no fresh trend) means resolve_pre_cool_modifier() falls through the
trend branch entirely and checks tomorrow_high(95) >= threshold_hot(85 default) — true,
so it returns HOT_DAY_PRE_COOL_MODIFIER=-2.0 instead of None.
compute_pre_cool_target(config, -2.0) = max(sleep_cool(72) + (-2.0), sleep_heat(64)+hysteresis(1)) =
max(70.0, 65.0) = 70.0 — 2F below the plain sleep band, not a no-op.
No nat-vent configured (natural_vent_delta absent) → pre-cool uses wake_time-4h fallback.
wake_time default = '06:30' → trigger at 02:30.
Assertion a2 (Issue #1441, added 0.9.9, owner re-sign): setpoint_writes (22:30, 02:30] == [70.0]. Without it a
deleted pre-cool write still passed: handle_pre_cool() emits pre_cool_applied (target 70) after the write
whatever its outcome, and a1 reads that event. Mutation-checked 2026-11-07: with the _apply_comfort_band() call
in handle_pre_cool() replaced by a no-write result, a2 fails on Tier A and real HA while a1 still passes.
Window: since = the bedtime write's own timestamp (22:30:00, excluded by the exclusive bound). Both tiers write
exactly 74 (14:00 classification; a use_coordinator run adds a 74 re-send at 14:04:59), 72 (22:30) and 70
(02:30); nothing re-sends the 72F ceiling between bedtime and the trigger (no midnight reclassification here,
unlike warming_trend_pre_cool_applied, whose window starts at its 00:00 reclassification).
use_coordinator is not needed (checked both ways): the engine-only run's direct handle_pre_cool() and the
coordinator's own 02:30 trigger (#1378 fire-time re-check, which real HA always runs) both reach the hot-day
gate, modifier -2.0 -> 70F, so the two paths agree. Unlike the warming-trend golden, no gate here depends on
which day the night is judged against: the 14:00 classification's today (91F) and tomorrow (95F) are both hot.

events.note: Plateaued heat wave: today 91°F, tomorrow 95°F — both hot, but only a +4°F trend (below the 5°F moderate threshold), so setback_modifier stays 0.0. The classifier never sees a fresh 'warming trend', only sustained heat.
Evening temperatures — AC holding indoor near comfort_cool.
Bedtime: normal sleep band [64/72] applied. Pre-cool fires separately at 02:30.

Pre-cool trigger fires (wake_time 06:30 - 4h fallback). setback_modifier=0.0 (no trend) but tomorrow_high=95 >= threshold_hot=85, so the hot-day fallback gate applies. Target = sleep_cool(72) + HOT_DAY_PRE_COOL_MODIFIER(-2.0) = 70F.

assertions.reason: Bedtime sleep band [64/72] — ceiling=72F for cool mode. Pre-cool has not fired yet; sleep setpoints are normal.

Pre-cool trigger fired via the hot-day fallback gate (Issue #558): setback_modifier=0.0 does not qualify via the trend branch, but tomorrow_high(95) >= threshold_hot(85) does, so resolve_pre_cool_modifier() returns HOT_DAY_PRE_COOL_MODIFIER=-2.0. compute_pre_cool_target() = sleep_cool(72) + (-2.0) = 70F, above the sleep_heat(64)+hysteresis(1)=65F floor, so it applies uncapped. Without this fallback the target would incorrectly equal sleep_cool(72) — a no-op — and this assertion would fail.

The thermostat is really told 70F, once, after the 22:30 bedtime write (72F) and up to the 02:30 pre-cool trigger. The pre_cool_applied row above reads the event's target, which is announced after the write whatever its outcome (even not_sent); this row reads the service call itself, so a lost, wrong or doubled pre-cool write fails (Issue #1441). No production re-send of the unchanged 72F ceiling falls in the window on either tier: the scenario has no midnight reclassification, and the bedtime write at 22:30:00 is excluded by the exclusive since bound.

verdict.summary: A plateaued hot-day forecast (no fresh warming trend, but tomorrow independently hot) still triggers overnight pre-cool banking via the new hot-day fallback gate
verdict.observed_behavior: classification_applied (day_type=hot, setback_modifier=0.0) → setback_applied (72F sleep ceiling) → pre_cool_applied (70F cool ceiling)
verdict.expected_behavior: Even without a fresh day-over-day warming trend, a household in a multi-day heat wave gets overnight thermal-mass banking every night tomorrow is forecast hot — not just on the one night the trend happens to jump.
